passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Chaptered House Engrossed text of HB2853, the version the House passed and the governor signed, printing the new section 15-2401.01.

rows.reasoning: Wilmeth co-sponsored HB2853 (2022) and voted Y on its House Third Reading, a single-subject Arizona empowerment scholarship account bill whose new section 15-2401.01 makes any resident "eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" in preschool-with-disabilities, kindergarten or "Any of grades one through twelve" a qualified student, which is universal eligibility. The account pays "Tuition or fees at a qualified school", a "nongovernmental primary or secondary school" barred only from discriminating "on the basis of race, color or national origin", so religious schools are not excluded and the money follows the student to the family's chosen school. That matches "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family"; the $2,200,000 appropriation funds administration only and is not an eligibility limit.
